title: Staged LTS rollout controller for Dedicated GPU pools
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Purpose: implement a staged Long-Term-Support (LTS) rollout controller and operator to orchestrate non-disruptive upgrades of Dedicated GPU pools. The controller must coordinate draining of GPU pools, interact with the autoscaler to prevent capacity erosion, enforce rollout gates (health, latency, error budget), and expose an operator API for rollouts, pause/resume, and emergency rollback. Scope: dedicated fleet only (reserved capacity), runtime binary upgrades, model-serving agent updates, and node-level driver/OS patching. Out of scope: hosted API multi-tenant routing changes and on-prem install automation (separate project).
acceptance_criteria: Controller can schedule a staged rollout across a cluster of GPU pools with a configurable batch size and inter-batch delay
During rollout, autoscaler prevents scale-in that would reduce committed capacity below a configurable floor
Each batch drain honors live request handoff with KV cache preservation for active sessions >1s
Rollout fails open and pauses if latency SLO or error rate breach thresholds are hit, with clear alerting to oncall
Operator exposes CLI/API to force-continue, pause, or rollback an in-progress rollout
End-to-end integration test in preprod demonstrating zero-data-loss for long-lived sessions and <5% p99 latency regression
implementation_notes: Architecture: controller will run in control plane and communicate with fleet agents via gRPC. It will annotate pool objects with rollout metadata and use leader election for safety

Draining behavior: implement a two-stage drain — (1) gentle drain: stop new allocations, gradual connection handoff, preserve KV caches for active sessions; (2) hard drain after grace period for stuck jobs
Autoscaler integration: add a Lease/Quota reservation API that the controller will call to temporarily pin capacity and request expansion in the target zone before draining starts
LTS channels: support channel metadata on release tags (lts-stable, lts-patch, preview). Controller will only pick images from allowed channels for a given fleet to respect customer pinning
Rollout gates: support metric-based gating (customizable metrics + thresholds) and manual approvals. Default gate set: p95 latency, error-rate (5xx), CPU/GPU utilisation, pod restart rate
Observability: emit per-batch events to Console rollout dashboard; include pre/post histograms for latency and token throughput
Compatibility: runtime must validate model-serving agent binary compatibility using a lightweight handshake before queueing a node for upgrade
CLI: redwoodctl rollout start|status|pause|resume|rollback with JSON output for automation
Backwards compatibility: when controller is not present, legacy rolling upgrades continue but without channel enforcement and capacity reservation
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (canary): upgrade single pool in non-critical region, run 6-hour smoke with synthetic and production-mirroring traffic
Stage 1 (limited): upgrade up to 10% of pools across different zones, run 24-hour gating checks
Stage 2 (ramped): increment batches by 20% with 1-hour observation windows until 80% coverage
Stage 3 (finish): remaining pools upgraded during low-traffic window with extended watch (48h)
Emergency pause: automatic if any gate trips OR manual via redwoodctl; on pause the controller will stop scheduling new batches and begin passive monitoring
rollback_plan: Fast rollback: redeploy previous image to last-upgraded batch and mark state as rollback_in_progress
Staged rollback: if fast rollback causes regressions, stepwise rollback with same gating rules as forward rollout
Fallback network policy: if KV cache incompatibility is detected, abort rollback and coordinate compatibility migration plan
Post-incident: capture diagnostic bundle (logs, kernel traces, agent metrics) and create retro ticket with RCA template
test_plan: Unit tests for controller state transitions (queued -> draining -> upgraded -> verified)
Integration tests in preprod that simulate autoscaler interference and validate reservation API behavior
Chaos test: randomly drop agent heartbeats during upgrade to validate graceful degradation
Performance test: measure p50/p95/p99 token latency across versions using production-like traffic for each batch
End-to-end test: run migration with large KV cache (multi-GB) to ensure cache handoff and fallback paths
metrics: Per-batch p50/p95/p99 latency delta compared to baseline
Active sessions impacted: count and percentage

2025-03-01 - Ravi Gupta: Implemented reservation API changes in autoscaler (PR linked). Need feedback from infra on leader election approach for multi-region control planes.
2025-03-03 - Priya Shah (SRE): Reviewed gating thresholds. Recommend lowering default p95 threshold to 1.2x baseline and add an early-warning threshold at 1.1x to avoid noisy aborts.
2025-03-04 - Ben Cho (Security): Confirmed no new elevated privileges required for controller aside from existing fleet-agent write annotations. Security review: low risk.
